units.translation: ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ are dochmiacs, but detached from one another; cf. on 149 and below on 837 ff. Further, at 785 ⟦3⟧ -- ~ - ~~~ -? The resolution is still in the way, for one cannot lengthen as with ---, nor insert a pause, which here would fall in the middle of a word. Pure dochmiacs remain if one (Paley) transposes ⟦4⟧ (instead of the manuscript reading, after Hermann and others) ⟦5⟧. Others restore a trimeter: ⟦6⟧ (⟦7⟧), or something similar, in which, however, the ā is striking. In v. 769 the bacchiacs (according to the metrical terminology) seem unambiguous, cf. ⟦8⟧, where likewise tetrameters; further on dochmiacs; at the close as at 170, see there.

779 ⟦1⟧ now for the third time in the same usage, see 150, 731. The sentence beginning with ⟦2⟧ (this word only here) has no continuation, since instead of a finite verb ⟦3⟧ follows; the scholiast explains this with ⟦4⟧ and cites the classic example from Homer 307, where the Aristarcheans similarly remark on ⟦5⟧ that either ⟦6⟧ is to be supplied, or this very enallage is to be assumed. Against this, Weil (1861) hit upon the very subtle idea of transposing verses; ⟦7⟧.. ⟦8⟧/ ⟦9⟧; ⟦10⟧; |⟦11⟧ (789f.) | ⟦12⟧, ⟦13⟧ |.. ⟦14⟧, by which the entire construction is put in order and, moreover, a correct sequence of thought is established. For if the Erinyes already now announce their vengeance, why afterwards the deliberation ⟦15⟧? Finally, ⟦16⟧ (790) is strange in its present surroundings; on the other hand, it is motivated and clear in the vicinity of ⟦17⟧ 781. This last, however, can also be resolved by emendation, and ⟦18⟧ may be more an exclamation of passion than deliberation; but the anacoluthon is precisely as such suited to the pathos, cf. on 94 ff. Weil himself also returned to the usual order.
but I, dishonored, wretched, heavy in wrath
I become unbearable to the citizens

782 ⟦1⟧ shows an epanadiplosis more frequent in Euripides than in Aeschylus; cf., however, also in the latter ⟦2⟧ 996, 1014, ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ 981, ⟦6⟧ 985, (⟦7⟧ 990, ⟦8⟧ 1000, etc. But the thought, with similar expression, already stood at 478; cf. also 801.
